framework: AWS Security Best Practices + PCI DSS v4.0 Mapping
description: Security incident detection via historical CloudTrail event analysis. Covers root activity, authentication anomalies, audit tampering, privilege escalation, and reconnaissance patterns.

items.title: Root account activity detected in audit period
items.description: The AWS root account was used to perform operations during the audit period. Root account usage bypasses IAM permission boundaries and audit controls, and is prohibited under PCI DSS.
items.remediation: Immediately investigate root account usage. Create IAM users/roles with least-privilege access. Enable MFA on root account. Consider removing all root access keys.

pci_dss.reason: All access must be based on least-privilege. Root account use violates least-privilege principle.
Shared/generic accounts (including root) must not be used for normal operations.
Root-level actions must be logged and reviewed as privileged access events.

items.title: Excessive failed console login attempts
items.description: Multiple failed console login attempts were detected, indicating a potential brute-force or credential-stuffing attack. Threshold: 5 or more failures in the audit period.
items.remediation: Enable MFA for all IAM users. Review and rotate credentials for affected accounts. Implement account lockout policies via SCPs. Consider enabling AWS Guard Duty for automated detection.

pci_dss.reason: Invalid authentication attempts must be locked out after no more than 6 attempts.
MFA required for all non-console admin access to protect against credential attacks.
Failed authentication attempts must be detected and responded to promptly.

items.title: CloudTrail audit trail tampering detected
items.description: Events indicating audit trail tampering were detected: StopLogging, DeleteTrail, or UpdateTrail. These actions can disable logging and allow malicious activity to go undetected.
items.remediation: Immediately investigate who disabled/modified logging and why. Re-enable CloudTrail. Apply SCPs to prevent trail deletion. Enable CloudTrail log file integrity validation. Set up alerts for trail modifications.

pci_dss.reason: Audit log files must be protected to prevent modifications.
Audit log files must be promptly backed up to a centralized log server.
Retain audit logs for at least 12 months with 3 months immediately available.

items.title: Privilege escalation events detected
items.description: IAM privilege escalation events were detected: unauthorized policy attachment, access key creation, or login profile creation. These actions can be used to gain persistent elevated access.
items.remediation: Review all IAM changes made during the audit period. Revoke unauthorized permissions. Implement IAM Access Analyzer. Apply least-privilege policies. Enable alerts for privileged IAM changes.

pci_dss.reason: All access privileges must be assigned based on minimum necessary access.
All user IDs and authentication credentials must be managed and reviewed regularly.
Use of and changes to identification and authentication mechanisms must be logged.

items.title: API throttling spike detected
items.description: An unusual number of API throttling errors (Throttling/RequestLimitExceeded) were detected. This may indicate automated scanning, enumeration activity, or misconfigured tooling.
items.remediation: Investigate the source of excessive API calls. Review service quotas and request limits. Check for automated tools making excessive calls. Consider enabling AWS Shield if DDoS is suspected.

pci_dss.reason: All actions taken by individuals with root or administrative privileges must be logged.
Security monitoring must include anomalous or suspicious activity detection.

items.title: IAM permission denial storm (AccessDenied spike)
items.description: A high number of AccessDenied errors were detected, indicating unauthorized access attempts, misconfigured permissions, or active reconnaissance of the environment.
items.remediation: Investigate principals generating AccessDenied errors. Review IAM policies for misconfiguration. Check for unauthorized principals attempting resource enumeration. Enable GuardDuty for automated anomaly detection.

pci_dss.reason: Invalid logical access attempts must be logged.
Failures of critical security controls must be detected, alerted, and reported promptly.

items.title: Unusual off-hours console logins detected
items.description: Successful console logins were detected outside business hours (before 07:00 or after 20:00 UTC). This may indicate unauthorized access or compromised credentials.
items.remediation: Investigate the off-hours logins and verify with the account owners. If unauthorized, immediately reset credentials and review activity performed during the session. Consider implementing time-based access controls via SCPs.

pci_dss.reason: Passwords/authentication factors must be changed if compromise is suspected.
All individual user access to cardholder data must be logged.
Security incident response must include monitoring for unusual access patterns.

items.title: Mass resource deletion detected
items.description: A high volume of Delete* API calls was detected during the audit period. This may indicate intentional data destruction, ransomware activity, or misconfigured automation.
items.remediation: Investigate the deletion events and verify authorization. Enable S3 versioning and MFA Delete. Enable AWS Backup for critical resources. Apply SCPs to restrict delete operations to authorized principals only.

pci_dss.reason: Audit log files must be backed up promptly to prevent data destruction from covering tracks.
Incident response plan must address data destruction scenarios.

items.title: Credential report accessed (reconnaissance indicator)
items.description: The IAM credential report was generated or downloaded during the audit period. This report lists all IAM users and their credential status. In attacker hands, it enables targeted credential attacks.
items.remediation: Verify that only authorized security personnel access credential reports. Restrict GenerateCredentialReport/GetCredentialReport to security audit roles only. Review what was done after the report was accessed.

pci_dss.reason: All user IDs and authentication credentials must be managed and reviewed — access to credential inventories must be restricted.
All changes to authentication mechanisms must be logged and reviewed.

items.title: Cross-account AssumeRole from unrecognized external accounts
items.description: Cross-account role assumption events were detected from external AWS accounts. These may indicate legitimate third-party integrations or unauthorized lateral movement between accounts.
items.remediation: Review all cross-account trust relationships. Ensure all external account IDs in trust policies are authorized. Apply conditions (aws:PrincipalOrgID, ExternalId) to cross-account trust policies. Audit and remove unused cross-account roles.

pci_dss.reason: All user accounts and access privileges must be reviewed at least once every 6 months.
Shared/service accounts must have documented use cases and be managed appropriately.
Hardware and software technologies must be reviewed every 12 months to confirm they continue to meet security requirements.

notes: MVP skill for CloudTrail historical event analysis. Detects active security incidents and anomalies that configuration-based skills cannot identify. Uses deterministic pre-checks (Tier 1) for all 10 controls — no LLM dependency for pass/fail decisions. Evidence distilled at collection phase to stay within 120K token budget.
